relevance.rationale: Argues that the AMPS firewall thought-experiment requires a quantum computation whose running time is exponential in the black-hole entropy, so the information behind the horizon is present but computationally inaccessible from outside. The corpus's information-theory chapter asserts a structurally identical thesis in categorical language across several blocks: rem:information-paradox-incompleteness ('existence without provability', degree-0 sections behind the horizon that no finite braid computation from outside produces, Bekenstein-Hawking entropy counting only degree-1 witnesses), thm:geometry-of-incompleteness, and rem:p-vs-np-event-horizon. Those blocks cite hawking1975, bekenstein1973 and goedel1931 and nothing from the complexity-of-decoding literature. Supporting, not core: this paper would change no derivation in the folio — it supplies prior art and independent physical corroboration for a claim the corpus presents as its own novel framing, which is a scholarly-honesty citation rather than a mathematical input. Corpus-grep over content/, docs/, computations/ finds no 'firewall'/'AMPS' and no complexity-theoretic black-hole reference.

keyResults.statement: A counting bound showing that decoding the relevant degrees of freedom out of the Hawking radiation requires a time exponential in the entropy, so for a wide class of black holes the experiment cannot be performed.
keyResults.useForFolio: External, physics-side precedent for the corpus's claim that degree-0 truth behind the horizon is unreachable by any finite computation from outside while degree-1 witnesses leak; lets rem:information-paradox-incompleteness state its position against the literature instead of alongside it.

keyResults.statement: The decoding task is recast as a quantum error-correction problem, and connected to zero-knowledge proof structure, to explain where the exponential comes from.
keyResults.useForFolio: The witnesses-versus-theorem framing of rem:p-vs-np-event-horizon (verifiable partial evidence accumulating toward a proof that never terminates) has a direct counterpart here; citing it grounds the analogy in an existing technical construction rather than leaving it as metaphor.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry; the corpus asserts horizon computational opacity as a framing contribution without engaging the literature that established the complexity-theoretic version.
rem:information-paradox-incompleteness cites only hawking1975, bekenstein1973, goedel1931 while claiming a computational-inaccessibility reading of the paradox.
rem:p-vs-np-event-horizon frames horizon opacity as a P-vs-NP-shaped claim with no reference to prior complexity-theoretic work on black-hole decoding.
